TACHIBANA Tatsuya
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal: To cultivate intelligence and originality, this course focuses on a philosophical text from another era and aims to improve reading comprehension and ability to think independently. Specifically, students learn to follow the structure of a text and identify the connection between claims and reasons. By discussing philosophical ideas with others, students learn to understand others’ ideas, think together, and develop critical thinking skills. Through these practices, students cultivate the thinking skills necessary for engineers who can think and act independently.
advice:
Course Description:
・In each class, students read a philosophical text and discuss a task assigned to their group. During the discussion, the instructor gives a short lecture and students take a short quiz based on the lecture. Students also formulate questions about the text. In the following week, after receiving the instructor’s answers to and explanations of those questions, each group prepares and submits a written response to the assigned task.
・A philosophical essay should be submitted at Class #10. Students choose one of the provided essay questions.
・A final report should be submitted after Class #14.

Expectations for Students:
・This course emphasizes accurate reading of texts (including reconstructing arguments), developing original thinking on that basis (including constructing your own arguments), and considering how philosophical methods can be applied to your own scientific or engineering research. Keep these aims in mind in group discussions, quizzes, and the philosophical essay.
・Look up unfamiliar terms on your own using an encyclopedia or a reference book.

activityGoals.body: To be able to understand philosophical ways of thinking and explain them concretely.
To be able to identify claims and reasons in texts written in different eras and with different assumptions.
To be able to analyze abstract questions, make them concrete, and develop your own answers.
To be able to express the process and results of thinking about the relation between technology and philosophy.
To be able to think critically about technology and philosophy and explain their relationship in clear writing.
To be able to self-evaluate the target abilities for students in this course.

achievementLevels.ideal:
1. Understanding philosophical ways of thinking and explaining them concretely in your own words.
2. Identifying claims and reasons in texts written by others from different eras and assumptions.
3. Making abstract questions concrete through analysis and answering them with appropriate reasons.
4. Expressing, in logical writing, the process and results of thinking with others about technology and philosophy.
5. Thinking critically about technology and philosophy and explaining it persuasively in clear writing.
6. Constantly evaluating your understanding of the course with the Target Abilities in mind.
achievementLevels.standard:
1. Understanding philosophical ways of thinking and explaining them concretely.
2. Identifying some claims and reasons in texts written by others from different eras and assumptions.
3. Analyzing abstract questions and answering them with reasons.
4. Expressing, in writing, the process and results of thinking with others about technology and philosophy.
5. Thinking critically about technology and philosophy and explaining it in clear writing.
6. Evaluating your understanding of the course to some extent with the Target Abilities in mind.
